title: Theoretical prediction of structural stability and superconductivity in T-hexagonal molybdenum dihydrides Monolayer
abstract: The realization of ambient-pressure, high-temperature superconductivity in hydrogen-rich materials remains a major pursuit in condensed-matter physics. While bulk hydrides require extreme pressures to stabilize, two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal hydrides offer a promising alternative to bypass these compression constraints. In this work, we investigate the structural stability, electronic properties, and phonon-mediated superconductivity of a hexagonal molybdenum dihydride (MoH2) monolayer using first-principles calculations. Total-energy evaluations reveal that the octahedral T-phase is energetically more favorable than the previously reported trigonal prismatic H-phase by 0.198 eV, establishing the T-phase as the true ground-state configuration. Consequently, we systematically evaluate the lattice dynamics and superconducting properties of this ground-state T-MoH2 monolayer within the frameworks of density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) and the anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg formalism. The transition metal-hydrogen vibrational networks induce strong electron-phonon coupling (EPC), yielding an integrated coupling parameter of λ= 1.04. Solving the anisotropic Eliashberg equations predicts a conventional superconducting transition temperature (Tc of 14.4K) at ambient pressure, characterized by a moderately gap distribution (Δ= 2.07-3.01meV at 5.0 K). Our findings highlight the T-MoH2 monolayer as a structurally, mechanically, and thermally stable platform for exploring low-dimensional conventional superconductivity under ambient conditions.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes the T-phase $	ext{MoH}_2$ monolayer, establishing it as a stable candidate for ambient-pressure superconductivity. Using first-principles calculations, the authors predict strong electron-phonon coupling ($\lambda=1.04$) leading to a conventional superconducting transition temperature of $14.4 	ext{ K}$. The findings position 2D hydrides as promising materials for low-dimensional quantum phenomena.
main_problem: The study investigates structural stability and phonon-mediated superconductivity in two-dimensional (2D) transition-metal hydrides to find ambient-pressure alternatives to high-temperature superconductors.
main_result: The T-phase of $	ext{MoH}_2$ is confirmed as the stable ground state, predicting a conventional superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$) of $14.4 	ext{ K}$ at ambient pressure.
method: The research employs first-principles calculations (DFT) combined with Density Functional Perturbation Theory (DFPT) and solving the anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg equations.
model_or_system: The system modeled is the hexagonal molybdenum dihydride ($	ext{MoH}_2$) monolayer, comparing its T-phase (octahedral) to a less stable H-phase (trigonal prismatic).
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), electron-phonon coupling parameter ($\lambda$), structural energy difference, and elastic constants.
important_parameters: Ambient pressure; $\lambda = 1.04$; $T_c = 14.4 	ext{ K}$; Energy stabilization of T-phase over H-phase ($0.198 	ext{ eV}$).
main_assumptions: The superconducting pairing mechanism is assumed to be conventional and mediated by phonons; the calculation uses a fixed Coulomb pseudopotential ($\mu^*=0.1$).
figures_summary: Figures detail structural comparisons (T vs H phase), thermal stability via AIMD, electronic structure (Fermi surface dominated by Mo $d$-orbitals), phonon dispersion/EPC spectral function ($\alpha^2F(\omega)$), and momentum-resolved superconducting gap closing.
paper_structure: The paper follows a logical progression: first establishing the ground state structural stability (T-phase vs H-phase); second, confirming mechanical and thermal robustness via elastic constants and AIMD; third, calculating electronic properties (metallicity) and phonon spectra; finally, applying the Eliashberg formalism to predict $T_c$.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter superconductivity, the rigorous application of advanced quantum many-body theory (Eliashberg equations) to a novel 2D material platform is methodologically rich for theoretical physicists.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Crystal structures of monolayer molybdenum dihydride (MoH2) in the (a) T-phase (octahedral coordination) and (b) H-phase (trigonal prismatic coordination). For each phase, the upper panel shows the side view along the a-axis (with the vertical thickness and c-axis indicated), and the lower panel shows the top view down the c-axis, where the unit cell is outlined by the black solid lines. Orange and pink spheres represent Mo and H atoms, respectively.

FIG. 3. Electronic structure of the monolayer T-MoH2. (a) Orbital- resolved electronic band structure along high-symmetry paths (left panel) and corresponding total and partial electronic density of states (EDOS, right panel). (b) Fermi surface topology across the first Bril- louin zone, highlighting electronic pockets surrounding the Γ, K, and M points. (c) Spatial distribution of the electronic charge density integrated within a narrow energy window around EF. (d) Planar- averaged electrostatic potential V(z) and local electric field E(z) pro- filed along the vertical z-direction across the monolayer plane.

FIG. 2. Thermal stability of the monolayer T-MoH2 from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations. (a) Time evolution of the total energy fluctuation per atom, E(t)−E0 (left axis, blue line), and temperature T(t) (right axis, orange line) over a 10 ps simulation run at 300 K. (b) Top-down snapshot of the 3×3×1 supercell structure of 27 atoms at the final step (10 ps) of the AIMD simulation. Orange and pink spheres represent Mo and H atoms, respectively.

FIG. 5. Phonon dispersion relations and electron-phonon coupling (EPC) properties of monolayer T-MoH2. (a) Phonon band structure along high-symmetry paths, where the color mapping indicates the strength of the mode-resolved EPC linewidth (γqν). (b) Phonon den- sity of states (PhDOS) projected onto the constituent Mo (blue) and H (orange) atoms. (c) The Eliashberg electron-phonon spectral func- tion α2F(ω) (black line) and the cumulative frequency-dependent EPC parameter λ(ω) (red line), yielding a total integrated value of λ = 1.04.

FIG. 4. Vibrational modes and simulated Raman spectrum of mono- layer T-MoH2 at the Brillouin zone center (Γ). (a) Schematic rep- resentation of the atomic displacement vectors for the four distinct optical phonon modes: Eu (947.3 cm−1), Eg (1048.1 cm−1), A1g (1200.1 cm−1), and A2u (1212.8 cm−1). Red arrows denote the direction and relative amplitude of atomic motions. (b) Smeared phonon mode profile representing the simulated high-frequency vi- brational spectrum, with peaks labeled according to their correspond- ing irreducible representations.
